Getting started with the beta version

TaktX has reached public beta phase. Join us in testing and evaluation and experience the high throughput performance that TaktX provides. 

Note, the engine and client are not feature complete and subject to change, but we are getting more stable. We use this period to get some battle experience and improve quality and performance based on your feedback. 

Prerequisites

Note the following prerequisites to run the engine:

  1. Understand the license terms of the public beta phase
  2. Docker & Docker compose 
  3. Have a running Kafka installation (included with the docker compose installation)
  4. JDK 21+ with Maven or Gradle to run the client
  5. Camunda Desktop Modeler to create your models

Run TaktX with Docker Compose

To start a complete TaktX environment locally:

  1. Download the artifact for TaktX Docker Compose, then extract it.

  2. In the extracted directory in a terminal, run:

    docker compose --profile full up -d
  3. Wait for the environment to initialize. Monitor the logs to ensure all components start. 
    # show the running containers
    docker     ps
    # Show the log of each container
    docker logs -f [Container id or name of the container]

The default docker compose file will start the following components:

  • Kafka for our persisted messages (port 9092)
  • Kafka UI, manage the Kafka topics (port 8085)
  • Grafana (port 3000) / Prometheus for metrics. It has a preconfigured dashboard 
  • The Taktx engine (port 8079(
  • The Console containing Runway, to monitor and administer process instances (port 3002)

After the applications have started succesfully you should see several topics being created in Kafka-UI. These topics are what drives the TaktX BPMN engine. All state is persisted in these topics. Open Runway by navigating to http://localhost:3002

Note: this docker compose file does not employ any authentication/authorisation so it is not recommended to run this in a production-like environment. Also it will not scale, for full scalability we will need an actual Kafka cluster and a separate set of Engine nodes
